#5074. BlackRock Launches Hong Kong Tokenized Fund With A HK$10 Entry Point

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

BlackRock has launched its first tokenized money market fund in Asia-Pacific, giving investors in Hong Kong a new way to move money between traditional investments and blockchain-based financial products.

The BlackRock tokenized fund, known formally as the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund, supports both conventional and tokenized investment units. It also introduces a use case for HKDAP, the Hong Kong dollar stablecoin issued by Standard Chartered-led Anchorpoint Financial.

The development follows Anchorpoint’s plans to expand HKDAP to Solana, announced in late October.

However, there is an interesting detail in BlackRock’s product disclosures. One of the fund’s tokenized classes requires a minimum investment of just HK$10, while access through stablecoins is reportedly limited to professional investors.

The technology may be making financial products more accessible, but the institutions behind them still decide who gets through the door.

BlackRock announced regulatory authorization for the fund on September 10, with its product listings identifying November 16 as the inception date. The commercial launch was reported on Tuesday, November 24.

Unlike many of the investment products available across decentralized finance, BlackRock’s fund does not depend on cryptocurrency lending, liquidity pools or token incentives to generate returns.

Its investment strategy revolves around short-term financial instruments, including government-backed securities and bank deposits.

Investors gain exposure to those assets through fund units. With tokenized units, blockchain technology is used to maintain ownership records.

BlackRock’s official product disclosure lists a minimum initial investment of HK$10 for its D OnChain class, alongside a management fee of 0.31% and daily income distributions.

For comparison, the fund’s conventional I class requires a minimum initial investment of HK$10 million.

The difference is substantial, although a lower investment minimum should not be confused with unrestricted access. Different share classes and distribution channels come with their own conditions.

Perhaps the most interesting part of BlackRock’s launch is what it means for HKDAP.

Anchorpoint Financial, a joint venture between Standard Chartered, Animoca Brands and HKT, received its stablecoin issuer licence from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in April.

Until now, much of the discussion surrounding regulated Hong Kong dollar stablecoins has focused on payments, transfers and their potential role in financial infrastructure.

BlackRock’s fund introduces another practical application. Eligible investors can use digital money denominated in Hong Kong dollars to access investments denominated in the same currency.

In its September announcement, BlackRock stated:

Imagine a company that already holds HKDAP for operational payments. Instead of leaving all its surplus liquidity in stablecoins, it could potentially move some of that balance into a money market fund and earn investment income while the money is not needed.

The important distinction is that the stablecoin itself is not generating the fund’s returns. The underlying financial instruments are.

For stablecoin issuers, this kind of integration could ultimately prove more valuable than simply securing another exchange listing. It gives businesses a reason to hold and use digital cash beyond cryptocurrency trading.

There is still a noticeable difference between what blockchain infrastructure can do and what BlackRock’s product currently offers.

The D OnChain class lists a daily dealing schedule with an 11 AM Hong Kong time trading deadline and settlement on the trade date.

Anyone familiar with decentralized finance will recognize the contrast. A blockchain does not stop processing transactions because a bank has closed or a fund has passed its dealing deadline.

But tokenizing an investment does not automatically change the operating hours, liquidity arrangements or legal obligations of the underlying fund.

BlackRock also warns that technology failures, compromised wallets and disruptions involving blockchain service providers could interfere with investors’ ability to access or redeem their holdings.

Restrictions on redemptions are possible under stressed market conditions, while investors remain exposed to potential capital losses.

These limitations are not necessarily a failure of tokenization. Institutional investors have regulatory, custody and accounting obligations that cannot simply be removed by deploying a smart contract.

Still, if investors ultimately have to work around many of the same deadlines and intermediaries they encounter in traditional finance, the immediate advantages of tokenization become narrower.

Earlier this month, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority expanded its EnsembleTX settlement initiative to support continuous settlement using tokenized central bank money.

The initiative involves several major financial institutions, including BlackRock, and supports applications involving tokenized deposits and investment funds.

These developments are gradually connecting different parts of the financial system that previously operated separately.

There are now regulated digital currencies, tokenized investment products and settlement infrastructure being developed to move value between them.

However, BlackRock’s latest launch also shows why the size of the tokenization market should not be measured solely by the number of financial products being brought onto blockchains.

The more interesting figures will be how much money actually enters these funds through digital cash, how frequently investors move between the two products and whether those transactions become cheaper or faster.

BlackRock’s product disclosures reviewed for this article did not yet provide usable figures for total fund assets or current yields.

Nor does the launch establish unrestricted access through decentralized exchanges or lending protocols.

Those are the developments worth watching before declaring that tokenized finance has moved beyond institutional adoption and into the hands of ordinary crypto users.

Hong Kong now has another piece of the infrastructure. The next challenge is getting people to use it.

#5073. Bitcoin (BTC) For $99,000? Bitcoin Refraction Model Puts a "Fair" Price

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Bitcoin's long-term trend value, based on various models like "Plan B", has been set ridiculously high, so chasing targets set by those models might not be the best decision out there, considering modern market conditions.

A revised Bitcoin Power Law model sets BTC's long-term price at $99,000, which is almost $50,000 below the $146,725 estimate that has been used by the traditional Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) model.

The creator of the newer, accordingly more accurate model believes the Bitcoin Power Law is still valid, but the fair value is certainly nowhere near the relevant market conditions.

One way or another, the newer models still set the current price threshold at one of the lowest historical levels in the history of the asset—approximately the 1st percentile of its distribution, which means that it stands among 60 of Bitcoin's daily closes that fell below this threshold.

The new model uses a completely different method for calculation: Quantile Regression instead of Ordinary Least Squares (OLS). The main difference is that OLS guesses Bitcoin's price trend based on its historical averages, while QR uses specific points in the price distribution, not an average. Essentially, the newer calculation model smoothens out extremes that made OLS less accurate.

Despite the newer calculation and estimation approach, the improved calculation algorithm and everything else, models are estimating, not making solid predictions.

There are thousands of other factors to consider when determining Bitcoin's next move, so any kind of model is useful only for evaluating the momentum and historical significance of the most recent movements.

The model also places its 0.1 percentile at $55,185, a level below which Bitcoin has closed only six times. The creator argues that only the lower part of Bitcoin's price distribution, between the 0.1 and 5th percentiles, may continue following the Power Law, while higher levels gradually move down towards this lower boundary.

The model also uses Protocol Time instead of Calendar Time. Still, its creator maintains that the Power Law is not broken. The problem, according to this view, is how previous models measured it and how much they allowed market bubbles to influence the results.

#5072. Best Crypto Wallets: Top 7 Picks for Max Security and Ease of Use

Home » Cryptopedia » Best Crypto Wallets: Top 7 Picks for Max Security and Ease of Use

Compare the top hardware and software crypto wallets to find your safest, easiest self-custody setup.

Keeping your cryptocurrency on an exchange is convenient, but it comes with risks. If the exchange gets hacked, freezes withdrawals, or runs into financial trouble, accessing your funds can become difficult. Using a self-custody wallet gives you direct control over your private keys and, ultimately, your crypto.

Whether you are holding Bitcoin for the next decade, trading memecoins on Solana, or exploring decentralized finance (DeFi), choosing the right wallet matters. Some wallets are designed to keep your assets as secure as possible, while others make it easier to trade, manage tokens, and connect to Web3 apps.

To help you find the right option, we’ve put together a list of seven popular crypto wallets, covering what each one does best, its main advantages, and what to consider before choosing it.

*Prices change frequently, so always confirm on the manufacturer’s official website.

If your primary goal is long-term wealth preservation, Ledger remains the industry benchmark for cold storage.

Unlike mobile apps that stay connected to the internet, Ledger devices store your private keys inside an offline, certified Secure Element chip, the same class of chip used in passports and credit cards (check Ledger’s website for the current certification details).

Through the Ledger Live companion app, you can buy, swap, and stake thousands of coins and tokens. Your private keys never leave the device. Ledger Live runs on your connected phone or computer, but transactions are signed on the Ledger itself.

For those who live by the motto “don’t trust, verify,” Trezor is the gold standard. Contrary to the competitors that keep parts of their code proprietary, Trezor’s firmware is fully open-source, meaning independent security researchers constantly audit it for vulnerabilities.

The Trezor Safe 5 pairs this transparency with a vibrant color touchscreen, haptic feedback, and an EAL6+ Secure Element. It also offers a dedicated Bitcoin-only firmware option for maximalists who want to minimize attack surfaces.

When it comes to interacting with decentralized applications (DApps), decentralized exchanges (DEXs), and NFT marketplaces, MetaMask is the undisputed gateway to Web3.

Available as both a browser extension and a mobile app, MetasMask connects seamlessly to virtually every Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) network, including Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Base, and BNB Chain.

Modern updates have expanded MetaMask beyond Ethereum via MetaMask Snaps and allow users to add support for non-EVM ecosystems like Bitcoin and Solana directly inside the same interface.

Originally built as the flagship wallet for the Solana ecosystem, Phantom has evolved into one of the fastest, cleanest multi-chain wallets on the market. Today, it seamlessly supports Solana, Ethereum, Base, Polygon, and Bitcoin in a single unified interface.

What sets Phantom apart is user experience. Transaction simulations show you exact balance changes before you hit approve, and its automated spam filter hides malicious airdrop NFTs so beginners don’t accidentally click phishing links.

If you want one smartphone app that holds virtually every cryptocurrency in existence without manual network configuration, Trust Wallet is built for you.

Supporting over 100 blockchains and millions of digital assets, it removes the technical friction of adding custom RPC networks or hunting down token contract addresses.

It also includes a built-in Web3 browser, straightforward in-app staking for major proof-of-stake coins, and an integrated Security Scanner that flags risky smart contracts.

Many newcomers confuse the main Coinbase exchange app with Coinbase Wallet, but they are completely separate products. Coinbase Wallet is a true non-custodial wallet—meaning you hold your own 12-word recovery phrase, and Coinbase cannot freeze or access your funds.

Note that the app’s branding has changed recently: Coinbase renamed it “Base App” in July 2025 and restored the Coinbase Wallet name in September 2026. It has since shifted toward multichain trading, including perpetual futures, prediction markets, and tokenized stocks, so some of its features are now aimed at more active traders.

Its biggest advantage is frictionless onboarding. You can link your exchange account to transfer funds into self-custody in seconds, claim a free human-readable username instead of copying long hexadecimal addresses, and explore Base and Ethereum DApps.

Traditional hardware wallets require cables, batteries, and carefully guarding a 24-word paper backup. Tangem reimagines cold storage as a sleek, waterproof smart card—roughly the size and thickness of a standard bank debit card.

To approve a transaction, you simply tap the card against the back of your NFC-enabled smartphone. Tangem comes in sets of two or three cards that act as physical backups for one another, allowing you to skip vulnerable paper seed phrases entirely (though a traditional seed option is still available if you prefer it).

Understanding the difference between hot and cold storage saves you from overpaying—or worse, leaving your funds exposed:

A common rule of thumb among experienced crypto investors is to use both, for example keeping around 90% of long-term holdings in a cold wallet and about 10% in a hot wallet for everyday trading and Web3 exploration. This is a guideline, not a standard – adjust it to your own situation.

With crypto, there’s no bank to call if something goes wrong. Transactions are usually irreversible, and if an exchange freezes withdrawals or goes bankrupt, your funds could be stuck for months or even years.

That’s why choosing the best crypto wallet matters. It gives you more control over your money and lets you manage your funds without relying on an exchange.

Your cryptocurrency is not stored inside the physical device—it lives on the blockchain. If your Ledger, Trezor, or Tangem card is lost, stolen, or broken, you can buy a replacement device and restore full access to your funds in minutes using your 12- or 24-word recovery phrase (or backup Tangem card).

While no system is 100% immune, cold hardware wallets cannot be hacked remotely because your private keys stay offline. Most wallet “hacks” happen when users accidentally sign a malicious smart contract on a phishing website or store their seed phrase digitally where malware can find it.

Software wallets like MetaMask, Phantom, and Trust Wallet are completely free to download and hold crypto in. Hardware wallets require an upfront purchase (typically $55 to $250). Regardless of the wallet you choose, you will still pay standard blockchain network (“gas”) fees whenever you send or swap tokens.

With a custodial wallet (like a standard exchange account), a third-party company holds your private keys and can freeze or restrict your withdrawals. With a non-custodial (self-custody) wallet, only you hold the private keys—meaning nobody can block your transactions, though you are solely responsible for backing up your recovery phrase.

No. Unlike traditional bank accounts, funds in a self-custody crypto wallet are not covered by government deposit insurance like the FDIC or SIPC. Because you act as your own bank, protecting your recovery phrase and verifying transaction details before approving them is your primary safeguard.

#5071. Does South Korea’s draft bill give banks control of won-backed stablecoins?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The South Korean FSC’s new draft bill could change things for the country’s crypto space. What’s what’s going on exactly?

Under the new plan, banks put together can own more than half of any won stablecoin issuer. A fintech company can still be the largest shareholder, but they can’t run the show alone anymore.

Issuers must have FSC approval and at least 5 billion won in equity. Reserves must cover 100% of tokens in circulation, and holders must be able to cash out at face value right away.

As far as exchanges go, one shareholder can hold 20% or 34% with FSC approval. They’ll also need separate licences for dealing, brokerage, and custody.

South Korea’s plan is a 22% tax on crypto gains above 2.5 million won a year. It was meant to kick in this January, but it looks like that date’s been pushed back to 2029.

One reason is that it’s the earliest Korea can start swapping crypto tax data with the United States.

If that happens, it won’t be the first delay. The tax was first proposed back in 2020 and has been shelved several times since.

Enforcement is still active though. AMBCrypto previously reported that 27 unlicensed exchange websites were blocked recently, including KuCoin, MEXC and BingX. This was after their apps were already restricted.

Users on those platforms are being nudged towards the country’s 28 licensed exchanges.

#5070. Microsoft’s ‘Code Red’ Exposes Crypto’s Own Cloud Problem

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Microsoft has reportedly declared a “Code Red” initiative to overhaul its engineering and crisis response following a global service outage that lasted approximately 24 hours. For an industry built around the idea of decentralization, crypto has good reason to pay attention.

According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters, the technology giant is reconsidering how it prevents and responds to major infrastructure failures after its November 12-13 outage disrupted businesses, government operations and financial firms.

Crypto likes to position itself as an alternative to centralized infrastructure. Yet some of its largest businesses depend on the same handful of cloud computing companies, and the consequences of that reliance have already been felt by traders.

In May, Coinbase experienced an infrastructure failure that demonstrated how surprisingly fragile access to cryptocurrency markets can be.

The exchange’s official incident report, published on June 1, traced the disruption to a cooling equipment failure inside an Amazon Web Services (AWS) data center.

Coinbase had five matching engine nodes located within the same building. Three went offline during the incident, leaving the system without enough functioning nodes to operate normally.

The exchange had not implemented an automated mechanism to switch its matching engine to another availability zone.

A separate failure involving AWS’s managed event-streaming infrastructure complicated the recovery further.

For approximately eight hours, customers experienced severe disruptions affecting trading, deposits and withdrawals. Restoring the remaining systems took roughly another 12 hours.

“The duration of the outage is unacceptable to us,” Coinbase acknowledged in its subsequent investigation.

This was not the first time the exchange had encountered such problems. An AWS outage in October 2025 resulted in three hours and 17 minutes of degraded performance for Coinbase customers.

Despite these incidents, the relationship between cryptocurrency businesses and cloud providers continues to deepen. More recently, Coinbase and AWS partnered to bring x402 payments to CloudFront publishers, bringing blockchain-based payments into existing web infrastructure.

The uncomfortable part is that the blockchains themselves did not need to fail for customers to lose access to exchange services.

A decentralized settlement network is of limited immediate use to someone whose assets are sitting inside an exchange they cannot access.

Moving assets away from centralized exchanges does reduce some of these risks. However, it does not necessarily eliminate reliance on centralized infrastructure.

When a user opens the application to check their balance or send a transaction, the wallet generally communicates with an Ethereum node through a remote procedure call, commonly known as an RPC.

That connection allows the application to retrieve blockchain information and submit signed transactions.

Many users rely on infrastructure operated by third-party providers rather than running their own nodes. If the provider becomes unavailable, the wallet may struggle to display balances or broadcast transactions, even while Ethereum continues producing blocks.

In an RPC service outage, the assets can remain intact on the blockchain even when the wallet’s usual connection to the network stops working.

Ethereum’s own node documentation acknowledges that widespread reliance on cloud hosting could introduce a common point of failure.

The distribution of Ethereum nodes also raises questions about infrastructure concentration. Having thousands of independently operated nodes does not necessarily eliminate shared dependencies if many rely on the same hosting providers.

Shared infrastructure can create security risks as well as availability problems. NewsBTC previously covered the debate over verifier and RPC security following the KelpDAO exploit. That incident was an exploit, not a routine cloud outage.

There are alternatives. Users can connect compatible wallets to another RPC provider or operate their own Ethereum nodes. Developers can also design applications to switch between independently operated infrastructure providers when one becomes unavailable.

But these options are not always obvious to the average person opening a wallet on their phone.

The industry has spent years making crypto easier to use, often by hiding much of its technical complexity. In doing so, it has sometimes reintroduced the dependencies that blockchain technology was intended to reduce.

It would be easy to criticize every cryptocurrency company that uses Amazon, Google or Microsoft infrastructure. The reality is more complicated.

Coinbase explained that keeping its matching engine nodes physically close together was a deliberate decision intended to meet the speed and capacity requirements of its markets.

Separating those systems introduces communication delays. Running redundant infrastructure also costs money, particularly when companies must synchronize large amounts of financial information across multiple locations.

Cloud computing providers offer considerable engineering resources and operational capabilities that smaller crypto companies would struggle to reproduce independently.

The problem is not simply that crypto businesses use centralized services. It is whether they have credible alternatives when those services fail.

Coinbase subsequently outlined plans to improve recovery across availability zones and conduct regular failover exercises in production environments.

Those are useful commitments, although publishing a recovery plan and successfully executing one during an unexpected outage are two different things.

There is no established evidence that Microsoft’s latest initiative was prompted by a failure of cryptocurrency networks. The relevance lies elsewhere.

As financial institutions bring more assets onto blockchains, the reliability of the infrastructure connecting investors to those networks becomes increasingly important.

A tokenized investment fund may exist on a distributed ledger, but investors can still depend on centralized custody providers, banking services, identity verification systems and applications to manage their holdings.

A decentralized exchange may execute trades through smart contracts, but its website and the infrastructure connecting users to those contracts can introduce separate vulnerabilities.

Crypto companies should be demonstrating how their products behave when their preferred infrastructure provider goes offline. Can users still submit transactions? Can traders cancel orders? Can another operator take over without waiting for an engineering team to intervene?

Microsoft’s reported response to its November outage is a reminder that even companies with enormous technical resources can discover weaknesses in systems they previously considered reliable.

Crypto does not need to abandon cloud computing. It needs to stop treating decentralization at the blockchain level as proof that everything built around it is equally resilient.

Ripple has once again landed a major partnership in Türkiye, but this time around with one of the country’s largest private banks, putting XRP in the spotlight.

While this comes as part of Ripple’s growing expansion into the traditional financial space, the blockchain firm announced it has partnered with Yapı Kredi, a major Turkish private bank, to support its cryptocurrency business.

As part of the partnership agreement, Ripple Custody will help the bank to securely manage its digital assets and provide custody services for its crypto trading platform dubbed Yapı Kredi Kripto.

While the partnership demands the full integration of the Ripple custodial infrastructure, the firm revealed that Ripple Custody will be installed on the bank's own premises.

This way, Yapı Kredi will have access to adequate security and control it needs to manage all digital assets on behalf of its customers, boosting its security.

The development is significant for the bank and the broader Turkish crypto market; it also marks a major milestone for Ripple as the firm claims to be the only custody service provider currently supporting leading Turkish banks licensed by the CMB as crypto asset custodians.

It is important to note that Türkiye currently stands as one of the world's top 10 retail crypto markets, with XRP recorded as one of its most widely used cryptocurrencies.

With Yapı Kredi now fortifying its position as a major player in Türkiye’s fast-growing crypto market, its partnership with the blockchain firm associated with XRP is likely to open new opportunities for XRP while positioning it for bigger adoption in the country.

#5068. VanEck is dropping Gemini from nearly $1 billion in Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana ETFs

Coinbase will remain the funds' custodian as VanEck ends its custody, clearing and staking arrangements with Gemini.

VanEck is ending its relationship with Gemini across three spot crypto ETFs, leaving Coinbase Custody as its remaining named custodian.

The asset manager disclosed in Nov. 19 regulatory filings that it had notified Gemini of plans to terminate its custody and clearing agreements for its Bitcoin ETF (HODL), Ethereum ETF (ETHV) and Solana ETF (VSOL).

The agreements are scheduled to expire in February 2027, and Gemini will continue to provide services until the termination takes effect. The decision also ends a separate arrangement under which Gemini facilitates Solana staking for VSOL.

The filings did not disclose the reasons for the termination or how much cryptocurrency VanEck currently holds with Gemini.

The three funds have attracted approximately $1.15 billion in cumulative net inflows since their respective launches and collectively managed $934.2 million in net assets as of Nov. 24, according to SoSoValue data.

VanEck's Bitcoin ETF accounted for the bulk of that exposure, with $977.1 million in cumulative net inflows and $848.2 million in net assets. Its Ethereum and Solana funds recorded cumulative net inflows of $151.6 million and $19.2 million, respectively.

VanEck's decision extends beyond asset safekeeping. Gemini also provides clearing infrastructure that helps the funds settle cryptocurrency transactions associated with ETF share creations and redemptions.

Under the existing arrangements, VanEck's funds can use Gemini Clearing to complete trades negotiated with liquidity providers that are also Gemini customers.

The service has supported cash-based orders, which require the funds to purchase or sell cryptocurrencies, and in-kind transactions involving the direct transfer of digital assets.

The scheduled February 2027 exit affects two services across VanEck’s HODL, ETHV and VSOL.

Coinbase Custody stays with all three funds. The filings name no successor to Gemini’s trade clearing service.

The lines track service appointments. The filings give no amount or timing for any transfers between custodians.

The connections trace each service described in the three November 19 termination filings across its scheduled effective date.

The lines track service appointments. The filings give no amount or timing for any transfers between custodians.

Coinbase will continue serving the Bitcoin and Ethereum funds under their existing prime broker agreements, while the Solana fund also maintains a separate custody agreement with the company.

Please enable JavaScript to verify and send this form.

VanEck did not identify a successor to Gemini's clearing services or provide a timetable for any cryptocurrency transfers between the custodians.

VanEck's decision contrasts with arrangements at other major US crypto ETF issuers that have established relationships with multiple digital asset custodians.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) uses Coinbase Custody as its custodian and has appointed Anchorage Digital Bank as an additional provider. Its latest quarterly report said the fund had no immediate plans to transfer Bitcoin to Anchorage.

BlackRock also maintains flexibility in its trading arrangements. The fund can execute Bitcoin transactions directly with third-party counterparties or through Coinbase Prime when processing cash-based creation and redemption orders.

Meanwhile, the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund maintains its primary custody and trade execution relationship with Fidelity Digital Assets, an affiliate of its sponsor. Fidelity has also appointed BitGo Bank & Trust as an additional custodian, although it reported no immediate plans to transfer Bitcoin to the company.

These arrangements allow BlackRock and Fidelity to retain additional custody providers without necessarily distributing their existing Bitcoin holdings across them.

VanEck's termination of Gemini's agreements moves in the opposite direction across three separate crypto investment products, increasing the importance of its remaining relationship with Coinbase.

Its September quarterly reports describe transactions conducted directly with liquidity providers, while earlier prospectuses also allowed alternative execution arrangements for certain trades if settlement failed.

Those existing arrangements could accommodate transactions previously handled through Gemini Clearing without VanEck appointing another dedicated clearing provider.

With the termination scheduled for February, VanEck's subsequent regulatory disclosures could reveal whether it intends to consolidate more of its trading infrastructure with Coinbase or establish new arrangements with other institutional service providers.

#5067. Bitcoin Falls as PCE Inflation Comes in Hotter Than Expected

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Falls as PCE Inflation Comes in Hotter Than Expected

Heavy ETF outflows, surging put bets, and fragile support leave traders watching whether a deeper slide is just beginning.

Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $60,000 on Wednesday, trading at around $58,220 as concerns about further losses grew ahead of Thanksgiving. The BTC price dropped 2.8% in 24 hours following the release of October inflation data, which showed that price pressures remained elevated according to the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation measure.

The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported that the October Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index rose 0.3% in October, matching September’s increase.

Core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy, climbed 0.3% on the month and 3.3% from a year earlier. Headline PCE inflation increased 3.8% from a year earlier.

The report also showed that US personal income rose 0.7% in October, while consumer spending increased 0.3%. However, real consumer spending was virtually unchanged, suggesting that higher prices continued to weigh on purchasing power.

Bitcoin price fell to about $55,300 over the weekend before recovering to around $64,400 on Tuesday on renewed stock market optimism after Nvidia reinstated its CEO, Jensen Huang.

However, the major crypto “acted as the canary in the coal mine”, according to Glassnode: BTC fully gave back the NVIDIA-driven rally within hours while stocks lagged, then came under pressure. Price broke the $62,000–66,000 support zone, retested summer lows, and is struggling to hold around the $60,000 level.

Bitcoin lost nearly 26% of its value over the past 30 days, and the realized losses are the heaviest since the FTX crash in November 2022.

In addition to that, approximately 90% of the tracked leveraged long positions between the previous week’s market price and Bitcoin’s realized price ($53,200) have been liquidated.

Glassnode suggests that much of the selling pressure is coming from the US. Over the past 20 trading days, US spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen around $4.3 billion in net outflows, marking one of their biggest periods of withdrawals since launch.

Spot market activity tells a similar story: over the past 30 days, US investors on Coinbase have been net sellers, while buying and selling on Binance have remained relatively balanced.

Glassnode’s latest data shows growing bearishness among Bitcoin options traders, with limited support against sharp price movements around current levels. Between $58K and $64K, options dealers are positioned in a way that could amplify volatility, potentially accelerating a sell-off if prices fall further.

Meanwhile, bearish bets are rising. Traders bought 1.7 put options for every call last week, the highest ratio since June 2022. Similar levels of pessimism appeared near Bitcoin’s 2022 market low, although prices continued falling for several more months.

Glassnode warns that Bitcoin’s current decline may not be over. Bitcoin price remains weaker than traditional equities, US buying demand is lacking, and the market is struggling to hold its summer lows.

Glassnode identifies $60,000 as a key level to watch. A decisive break below it, followed by a close under $58,500, could open the door to a decline towards $53,200.

A recovery above $60,000, supported by renewed spot Bitcoin ETF inflows, would offer stronger evidence that the market is stabilising.

#5066. Top 8 Decentralised Exchanges to look out for in November 2026

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Decentralised exchanges, or DEXs, use smart contracts or liquidity pools to facilitate cryptocurrency trading. Users are at the core of DEXs, as they retain complete control over their assets and do not need to depend on centralized exchanges to protect their funds or process their withdrawals. DEXs let users maintain ownership of their private keys and also reduce the risk of custody failures.

Here is our list of the top 8 decentralized exchanges in the space that users can trade on:

Pancake or PancakeSwap is one of the most popular DEXs on the BNB Chain and was created to provide users with a low-cost, accessible alternative to Ethereum-based decentralized exchanges.

The platform recently rebranded from PancakeSwap to Pancake, dropping “Swap” as it expanded from a single-chain token-swap DEX to a multi-chain liquidity hub spanning 11+ blockchains, and added perpetual futures and 24/7 tokenized stocks and ETFs.

Uniswap introduced the Automated Market Maker (AMM) model that changed how cryptocurrency trading could take place without any central intermediaries or traditional order books. Users could swap tokens directly from their wallets across Ethereum and other blockchains.

The platform also allows users to earn rewards through peer-to-peer trading, and the open-source architecture has influenced others in the space, making it an important reference point for the DEX industry.

Raydium leverages Solana’s high-speed blockchain infrastructure, combining AMM, liquidity infrastructure, and token trading functionality. This is useful not just for DeFi users but also for retail users.

Users can trade and exchange their assets directly through their wallets. The tools on Raydium help new projects establish liquidity and attract traders. RAY is the native token of the platform and is useful with governance and incentives on the platform.

Hyperliquid has an order book that runs on-chain instead of an AMM, giving users a centralized experience. The platform is especially known for its perpetual futures and spot trading services, whereas the ecosystem itself supports borrowing, lending, and real-world assets.

The platform is a Layer 1 chain and consists of 2 main components: HyperCore and HyperEVM. HyperBFT is the consensus mechanism used underneath to support both. Stop, limit, and margin orders are all supported on Hyperliquid. HYPE is the native token of the platform.

Balancer is a DEX protocol built on Ethereum that supports multi-token liquidity pools and yield-bearing assets. Token pairings can be customized with multiple assets, unlike the traditional 50/50 pairings. It functions more like an automated portfolio manager, customizing token weights, creating pools with adjustable weight ratios, and letting users set their own trading fee.

The platform provides a level of flexibility that lets users and liquidity providers create specialized trading environments and program them as per their needs.

SushiSwap was launched as a fork of Uniswap in 2020 and lets users trade through liquidity pools instead of traditional order books. These users can either be Traders or Swappers or users who want to exchange one cryptocurrency for another; or Liquidity Providers who supply assets to liquidity pools to conduct trades.

The platform uses a multichain approach and supports various blockchain networks, letting users access different DeFi environments. The native token of the platform is SUSHI, which is useful in governance and incentive-based applications.

Orca lets users swap and conduct transactions at lightning fast speeds. Whirlpools are the platform’s concentrated liquidity pools that let liquidity providers provide capital within selected price ranges instead of distributing it uniformly across a price curve.

Orca is the native token of the platform. The platform’s simple interface appeals to a lot of traders. Wallet-to-wallet trading of SPL tokens is also a viable option for users.

Meteora is a liquidity protocol built on Solana focusing on providing advanced liquidity management and supporting token swaps. Dynamic Liquidity Market Maker or DLMM is a major feature of the platform allowing liquidity providers to allocate assets across different price bins.

Liquidity providers get to concentrate their assets around selected trading prices and various liquidity pool configurations can accomodate various market conditions and trading strategies. Meteora also supports emerging token projects and liquidity tools that can be helpful to establish trading markets and manage liquidity.

Decentralised exchanges are an essential part of the crypto and DeFi ecosystem. DEX platforms give users an extra level of control over their assets when they buy, sell, exchange or manage their assets.

While every trader has their own requirements, the best platform would depend upon individual needs, preferred networks, trading pairs and risks. Users should do their own research before investing.

#5064. Prop Firm Payouts Near $2 Billion: 10 Best Prop Firms In 2026

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Prop firm payouts are approaching the $2 billion mark, with data from Payout Junction showing nearly $1.97 billion in cumulative payments across 45 tracked firms since October 2023. More than $115 million has been recorded in November 2026 alone.

The figures offer a glimpse into how large the funded trading industry has become. But finding the best prop firms in 2026 requires looking at something payout leaderboards rarely tell you: what traders actually have to go through to get paid.

A $100,000 futures account with a $3,000 maximum drawdown gives a trader just $3,000 of room for error. Add consistency requirements, withdrawal caps and restrictions on trading strategies, and two accounts with identical advertised balances can offer very different trading conditions.

The industry is also expanding beyond its traditional forex and futures markets. New platforms are introducing prop trading for cryptocurrencies and tokenized stocks, giving traders access to a wider range of markets without having to commit the full advertised account balance themselves.

For this guide, we examine ten prop firms across forex, futures and cryptocurrency markets, looking beyond advertised profit splits to compare evaluation rules, trading conditions, costs and payout eligibility.

Editorial disclosure: This guide is based on published trading rules, product documentation and available payout data. Traders can lose their challenge fees, and most retail funded trading programs initially use simulated accounts. Receiving a payout is not guaranteed.

The firms are grouped by their suitability for different trading styles rather than ranked by a single payout leaderboard.

According to Payout Junction’s November 24 data, approximately 1.19 million payout transactions have been matched to public blockchain records since October 2023.

The tracker covers 45 firms, although its figures do not necessarily represent all payments made by those businesses. Bank transfers and other payments outside its blockchain tracking coverage may not appear in the dataset.

November has already recorded roughly $115.5 million in tracked payments across more than 91,000 transactions.

These are substantial figures, but they need context.

A firm paying out $50 million does not necessarily offer a better opportunity than one paying out $5 million. The larger business could simply have more customers, higher fees or a larger number of accounts.

Chart by NewsBTC, data from Payout Junction, November 16–22, 2026. Tracked blockchain payments only.

Nor do the figures tell us how much traders collectively spent on challenges, resets and subscriptions before receiving those payouts.

Without that information, it is impossible to determine the industry’s aggregate profitability for traders.

Payout data is useful evidence that payments have occurred. It is not evidence that the average customer makes money.

That distinction matters when comparing the following firms.

FTMO offers a conventional two-phase evaluation for traders who prefer clearly defined profit objectives and fixed overall loss limits.

Its two-step model requires a 10% profit target during the first phase and 5% during verification.

The maximum daily loss is 5% of the initial simulated capital, while the overall loss limit is 10%.

For a $100,000 evaluation, that translates into a $10,000 first-phase profit target and a $10,000 maximum overall loss allowance.

FTMO also offers a separate one-step model. Traders should not assume that its rules are identical to the traditional challenge.

The two-step structure may appeal to traders whose strategies require more breathing room than accounts with narrow trailing loss limits.

The first-phase target, however, requires meaningful performance relative to the allowed drawdown.

FTMO is worth considering for traders with an existing, tested forex or CFD strategy. Its two-step structure is easier to assess mathematically than many trailing-drawdown alternatives, although that does not make it easy to pass.

FundedNext operates across CFDs and futures, offering several routes to funded-style trading.

Its Stellar 2-Step model is particularly interesting for traders who want a traditional evaluation with relatively conventional risk limits.

The first phase requires an 8% return, followed by 5% in verification. Both phases apply a 5% daily loss limit and 10% maximum overall loss.

The published rules specify five minimum trading days per phase.

The firm also offers alternative CFD challenge formats and futures evaluations.

One area worth examining is its performance reward policy. Reward frequency and eligibility can vary according to the option selected, with some routes requiring a specific number of profitable trading days.

This makes comparing the headline profit split alone insufficient.

FundedNext’s strongest feature is choice. Its biggest complication is also choice. Traders should compare the funded-stage conditions of each product before deciding which evaluation to purchase.

FundingPips offers several evaluation models, including one-step, two-step and evaluation-free alternatives.

Its 2-Step Standard model requires an 8% profit target followed by 5% in verification.

The firm’s current documentation also confirms that the previous optional 10% first-phase target was discontinued on July 24, 2026.

FundingPips is an example of why traders must pay attention to changes in prop firm rules.

Its Standard model documentation applies a 35% consistency condition to the on-demand reward cycle.

This means a trader who generates most of their profit during one unusually successful session could need additional trading before qualifying for a withdrawal.

That might suit a strategy producing relatively steady returns. It could be less suitable for traders whose profits are concentrated around a handful of strong market opportunities.

FundingPips deserves consideration for its payout flexibility, but traders should examine the conditions attached to their preferred withdrawal cycle rather than choosing whichever option advertises the highest reward share.

The5ers offers several forex-focused evaluation and account-development programs.

Its High Stakes program is built around a two-stage evaluation and subsequent growth opportunities.

The firm distinguishes between different versions of High Stakes, making it important to identify the exact account being purchased rather than relying on older comparisons.

The appeal of The5ers is its focus on account development over time.

Traders who already have a strategy capable of producing steady returns may find growth-oriented programs more interesting than accounts designed primarily around rapid evaluations.

However, scaling opportunities should not be treated as guaranteed increases in accessible trading capital.

The trader must meet the conditions attached to the program, and trading restrictions continue to apply.

The5ers is a reasonable candidate for patient forex traders who value gradual account development. Its suitability depends on the precise High Stakes version and the trader’s ability to satisfy its growth criteria.

Hola Prime offers multiple evaluation formats across forex, CFDs and futures.

Its 2-Step Prime challenge requires an 8% profit target during the first phase and 5% during the second, with at least three trading days in each phase.

The firm’s published schedules also differentiate risk limits according to account size.

Hola Prime’s product range gives traders alternatives to the standard evaluation experience. However, account fees, platform access and withdrawal terms differ across models.

Its advertised challenge-fee refund also comes with conditions. Under the reviewed 2-Step Prime terms, the refund is distributed across the first four successful payouts rather than returned immediately upon passing.

That is an important detail for anyone calculating how much they need to earn before recovering their initial expenses.

Hola Prime is worth comparing if trading platform choice matters to you. Just remember that a fast payout-processing promise begins after a withdrawal becomes eligible, not necessarily after your first profitable trade.

Topstep is focused on futures trading through its Trading Combine and subsequent funded-account structure.

Unlike a traditional CFD evaluation, the maximum loss allowance is relatively small compared with the advertised account size.

Its published Trading Combine parameters include maximum loss limits of $2,000 for a $50,000 account, $3,000 for a $100,000 account and $4,500 for a $150,000 account.

A trader purchasing the $50,000 option is not receiving $50,000 that can be lost while testing a strategy. The relevant initial risk allowance is $2,000.

After passing the Trading Combine, traders can progress to an Express Funded Account, which is a simulated funded-stage account.

Its payout policy includes conditions relating to withdrawal eligibility, payout limits and changes to the maximum loss threshold after withdrawals.

Topstep is worth considering for futures traders who prefer a structured environment. Anyone moving from forex prop trading should first understand how dollar-based trailing loss limits differ from percentage-based static drawdowns.

Tradeify offers futures evaluations with different routes into funded-stage trading.

Its Select evaluation does not impose a daily loss limit during the evaluation but does apply a consistency requirement.

After passing, traders choose between Select Flex and Select Daily payout policies.

The ability to select a payout arrangement is attractive because not every trader earns profits in the same way.

A trader producing relatively consistent daily returns may prefer a different structure from someone whose strategy depends on occasional larger moves.

However, the choice is permanent for that funded account, according to Tradeify’s official payout policy.

Changing to the alternative arrangement requires obtaining another qualifying account.

Tradeify’s Select model is particularly interesting because it allows traders to choose how they want to approach withdrawals after evaluation. That flexibility is only valuable if the trader understands both options before selecting one.

Take Profit Trader offers futures trading programs built around an evaluation, a simulated PRO account and potential progression to a live-market PRO+ account.

The firm published updated plan information on November 23, 2026, making older descriptions of its account rules particularly important to recheck.

Its current product announcement describes three-day evaluations, frequent PRO withdrawals and no funded-stage consistency rule under the new plans.

The buffer is the detail traders should examine most closely.

The firm allows eligible traders to withdraw profits above the required buffer. Consequently, a trader can have a profitable account without necessarily being able to withdraw all that profit while retaining the account.

Legacy accounts may also remain subject to their original terms.

Take Profit Trader stands out for its withdrawal model. Traders interested in frequent payouts should still calculate how much profit must remain in the account before treating those earnings as spendable income.

Lucid Trading offers several futures account models, including LucidPro, LucidFlex, LucidDirect and LucidDaily.

Its LucidFlex program is particularly relevant to traders who want to avoid funded-stage profit-concentration restrictions.

According to the firm’s LucidFlex documentation, the funded account does not impose a consistency rule or a separate payout buffer.

The published profit-sharing arrangement is 90% for the trader.

The absence of a consistency rule does not mean traders can withdraw unrestricted amounts whenever they choose.

LucidFlex still has specific payout conditions, including requirements that must be satisfied before a withdrawal is approved.

Traders must also consider how a payout affects the account’s maximum loss threshold.

LucidFlex may appeal to traders who dislike having their profitable sessions constrained by a consistency formula. That makes the account more flexible in one respect, not necessarily less risky overall.

HyroTrader focuses on cryptocurrency traders rather than adapting a traditional forex evaluation to include a limited selection of digital assets.

Its one-step program requires a 10% profit target, with a 4% daily drawdown and 6% maximum overall loss under the published model.

The firm also offers alternative evaluation formats, including its recently introduced lower-cost Hyro Core program.

The attraction is that traders can use crypto-oriented trading infrastructure and market data rather than relying exclusively on a conventional forex platform.

For traders unfamiliar with derivatives, our guide to long and short positions in crypto explains how leverage and liquidation affect market exposure.

HyroTrader’s trading rules also clarify that allocated challenge and funded-account balances are simulated. Payouts represent a contractual share of eligible simulated trading performance.

That distinction matters because the term funded account is frequently misunderstood.

HyroTrader is worth examining for traders who already specialize in crypto markets. It is less compelling for someone whose only reason for choosing crypto is the belief that higher volatility makes a challenge easier to pass.

There is no single account structure that suits everyone.

These selections reflect specific published product features, not independently measured payout approval rates or guarantees of superior results.

The advertised account balance is usually one of the least informative numbers in a prop firm comparison.

Account A offers twice the advertised balance of Account B. Yet it provides less room for losses and requires a substantially higher profit relative to that allowance.

This does not establish the probability of passing either challenge. That depends on the strategy, trading costs, risk management and other account rules.

It does show why choosing the largest advertised account is not always sensible.

The calculation becomes more complicated when an account uses trailing drawdown.

A static maximum loss threshold remains anchored to a specified balance under the account’s rules.

A trailing drawdown moves upward as the trader generates profits, potentially reducing the room available for a subsequent losing streak.

Intraday trailing drawdown is particularly important because some models adjust the threshold based on unrealized profits.

A trade that briefly gains $1,000 before closing with a much smaller profit can therefore affect the trader’s remaining loss allowance.

Two firms advertising the same maximum drawdown can offer very different practical conditions depending on how and when that threshold moves.

Passing an evaluation is generally only the first stage.

The rules that determine whether someone receives a withdrawal can be more restrictive than the initial profit targets.

A consistency rule limits how much of the qualifying profit can come from a single trading session or another defined period.

For example, suppose a trader earns $2,000 during their best day and finishes the payout cycle with $4,000 in qualifying profit.

That best day represents 50% of the total.

Under a hypothetical 40% consistency requirement, total qualifying profit would need to reach at least $5,000, assuming the best day remains unchanged and the rule uses this particular calculation.

The trader may have to continue trading even though they are already profitable.

Some firms require profits to remain in an account as a buffer against future losses.

Others limit how much traders can withdraw during their initial payout cycles.

These restrictions are not necessarily unreasonable. A firm may want traders to demonstrate sustained performance before allowing larger withdrawals.

But customers should know exactly what they are buying.

There is a considerable difference between advertising daily payouts and allowing a trader to withdraw every dollar earned that day.

Account agreements can restrict copy trading, certain automated strategies, cross-account hedging, account sharing, news trading and other trading behaviors.

The precise definitions differ between firms.

Before paying for an account, traders should review both the public trading objectives and the account agreement governing payout eligibility.

A strategy permitted during evaluation may have different conditions after funding.

The advertised challenge price is only the initial expense.

Depending on the firm and product, customers may also incur subscription charges, reset fees, funded-account activation fees, market-data fees, platform costs or withdrawal-processing charges.

Promotional discounts can make the first purchase attractive without necessarily reducing the cost of subsequent attempts.

Consider a hypothetical trader who purchases four $100 challenges before successfully qualifying for a funded account. That trader has spent $400 before accounting for any additional charges.

The first $300 payout would not mean the trader has made a net profit from prop trading.

Their total challenge expenditure would still exceed their withdrawals.

This is another reason the industry’s approaching $2 billion payout milestone should not be confused with $2 billion in net trader earnings.

Our editorial assessment considers the following factors:

The selection is based on documentary research rather than a claim that NewsBTC has personally purchased, traded or withdrawn money from every program.

Reported payouts are considered supporting evidence of industry activity, not a standalone measure of reliability.

Retail prop firms generally offer traders access to an evaluation or simulated trading program in exchange for a fee.

Belgium’s financial regulator, the FSMA, has also published a consumer warning about retail prop trading programs, highlighting the risks of paying for repeated challenges.

Participants who meet the contractual requirements may receive monetary rewards linked to their trading performance. Some businesses subsequently move qualifying traders into live-market accounts.

This is different from opening a conventional brokerage account with personal deposited trading capital.

It also means traders should examine who operates the program, which legal entity they contract with, where disputes are handled and what happens if the provider changes its rules or ceases operations.

A large number of successful payout transactions does not guarantee that every valid withdrawal will be approved, nor does it establish the financial health of the company.

Before buying a challenge, traders should read the current agreement, establish their eligibility and understand which circumstances can lead to account termination.

FTMO and FundedNext are worth comparing for traditional forex evaluations. Topstep, Tradeify, Take Profit Trader and Lucid Trading offer different futures trading structures, while HyroTrader is focused on cryptocurrency.

The most suitable firm depends on the trader’s strategy, risk tolerance, market preference and withdrawal requirements.

Take Profit Trader offers daily eligible withdrawals under its reviewed PRO model, subject to the required buffer. Tradeify also offers a Select Daily payout arrangement.

Daily availability does not remove other eligibility conditions.

LucidFlex does not impose a funded-stage consistency rule under its published terms. Take Profit Trader’s new PRO plans also advertise no funded-stage consistency requirement.

Evaluation-stage restrictions may still apply.

HyroTrader is one of the crypto-focused firms worth researching because its programs are built around digital-asset trading.

Traders should compare cryptocurrency market access, drawdown calculations, exchange integrations and payout eligibility before selecting a program.

Yes. Traders can lose evaluation fees, subscriptions, reset fees and other charges without ever receiving a payout.

The simulated nature of many funded accounts does not eliminate the financial risk of paying for repeated evaluations.

No. Withdrawals depend on the firm’s contractual requirements, trading-rule compliance and ability to make payments.

Historical payout figures do not guarantee future withdrawals.

The prop trading industry has grown considerably, and nearly $2 billion in tracked payouts demonstrates that substantial sums are changing hands.

What it does not demonstrate is how many traders are profitable after accounting for their expenses.

The best prop firm is not necessarily the one paying the most money, offering the largest account or advertising the highest profit split.

It is the one whose evaluation and funded-stage rules are compatible with a trader’s existing strategy.

Before purchasing a challenge, calculate how much room the account actually provides for losses, how much profit must be generated before a withdrawal becomes possible and how much repeated attempts could cost.

Those numbers are considerably more useful than the advertised account balance.

Bitcoin [BTC] has slipped below the $60k mark for the second time within a week. According to CoinMarketCap data, the leading crypto was down 26.1% over the past month and 8.5% over the past week.

The rally past $80k in September fueled hopes of a bullish reversal, and it was widely accepted that the cyclical bottom might be in. Unfortunately for holders and investors, the rally didn’t last.

Relative weakness, like relative strength, is something market participants must be keenly aware of. An altcoin rallying while the rest of the market consolidates is a sign of relative strength and a good bet for continued momentum.

Equally, Bitcoin’s sell-off from the bounce to $64,603 on Monday, the 23rd of November, was worth noting.

Glassnode pointed out that stocks jumped on the news that NVIDIA reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Yet, within six hours of the 5% bounce, Bitcoin had retraced the move, and since then, has slipped below the $61k local support zone too.

The stock markets have also come under pressure. Nasdaq’s gains since the news came are gone. Investors are using any shred of strength to sell into, and Bitcoin was only the canary in the coal mine, wrote Glassnode.

Add to this a persistent lack of demand, and a BTC slide to $53k or even lower seems viable. In the past 20 trading days, U.S. spot BTC ETFs have shed $4.3 billion. Coinbase saw heavy selling pressure.

U.S. investors are wary of further drawdown, the data showed.

The short-term holder spent output profit ratio (STH SOPR) was at 0.99. Readings below 1.0 meant coins of this group are, on average, moving at a loss.

Crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. observed that the LTH SOPR had fallen by 0.20 over the past week. It reached a 90-day low at 0.76, revealing LTH-moved coins were, on average, at deeper losses than the STH coins.

An SOPR return above 1.0 would signal the cohort’s profitability. Yet, the 22-day below-break-even LTH SOPR streak, alongside the BTC weakness and lack of demand, was a worrisome signal.

Alphractal data showed that the onchain realized price of Bitcoin was $53,104. If these bearish conditions persist, a price drop to $53k could materialize.

#5062. Bitcoin’s crash protection could make its next selloff worse as US inflation data looms

Options dealers could amplify price swings between $58,000 and $64,000, even after much of Bitcoin's vulnerable futures leverage has been cleared.

A Bitcoin put can cushion losses for its buyer, while the trades a dealer makes to hedge the same option can make a fresh selloff harder to stop.

In its Nov. 24 report, Glassnode estimated that options dealers could reinforce declines by selling and rallies by buying when Bitcoin traded between $58,000 and $64,000. The US inflation report due Nov. 25 gives that setup a near-term test.

On a seven-day average, 1.7 Bitcoin puts traded for every call, the highest ratio since June 2022, according to Glassnode’s Nov. 24 report.

The put-to-call ratio for outstanding contracts separately reached its highest since May 2021. Put trading includes sellers and positions that serve purposes beyond crash protection, so the volume ratio shows where activity shifted without revealing who took which side.

A put gives its buyer the right to sell at a fixed price, or receive the equivalent cash payoff. The lower Bitcoin finishes below that price, the larger the payoff before the option's cost.

A dealer who sells the put takes the other side of that exposure and can hedge by selling Bitcoin or futures. As Bitcoin falls, the put becomes more sensitive to the decline, and the dealer may need to sell more to keep the hedge balanced.

Gamma measures how quickly an option’s price sensitivity changes. If prices reverse, a dealer in short gamma can buy back part of the hedge, adding to the rebound.

The feedback can be stronger when few buyers or sellers stand ready to take the other side, a pattern that researchers studying equity options found in less liquid stocks.

Glassnode estimated positive dealer gamma in the adjoining $56,000-$58,000 and $64,000-$66,000 bands. Dealers hedging positive gamma can buy weakness and sell strength, helping absorb a move. Those were modeled zones for one snapshot, and new trades or expiries can shift them.

A separate estimate from GEX Monitor from Nov. 24 also showed negative net gamma near $60,000, with the largest concentration by absolute exposure at that strike.

Glassnode’s Nov. 24 estimate put short gamma between $58,000 and $64,000. Bitcoin was near $59,700 later that day.

Within the estimated short-gamma band, dealer hedges can reinforce both a selloff and a rally.

The bands describe an estimate at one point in time. Dealer positions, liquidity and the influence of hedging can change as prices move, trades arrive or contracts expire.

Range widths are proportional to the reported dollar spans. Glassnode’s estimates use Nov. 24 data at 16:00 UTC. The later CryptoSlate observation at 21:12 UTC is rounded to $59,700. The paths illustrate short-gamma dealers hedging a move.

The bands describe an estimate at one point in time. Dealer positions, liquidity and the influence of hedging can change as prices move, trades arrive or contracts expire.

Glassnode estimated that nearly 90% of the leveraged futures longs it had flagged between the prior week’s Bitcoin price and its realized price had cleared. Realized price is the average price at which coins last moved.

Please enable JavaScript to verify and send this form.

The selloff had already pushed into a $55,000-$62,000 cluster of positions at risk of liquidation.

Futures liquidations occur when traders can no longer meet their margin requirements, so options dealers rebalance as prices move even if nobody faces a margin call.

Glassnode reported $4.3 billion of net outflows from US spot Bitcoin ETFs over the 20 trading days covered in the report.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis scheduled its October inflation report and revised third-quarter GDP for Nov. 25 at 8:30 a.m. ET. The inflation report includes the personal consumption expenditures price index (PCE).

Trading Economics listed a 0.3% monthly consensus for core PCE, which excludes food and energy. The Cleveland Fed’s model estimated 0.27% separately.

Investors are watching what the data means for rates after the Fed’s October minutes showed broad support for more tightening if the economy evolved as officials expected.

At derivatives exchange Deribit, Wednesday’s daily Bitcoin options are scheduled to expire at 3 a.m. ET, five and a half hours before the release.

They had about 6,172 BTC of open interest, around 1.4% of outstanding coin-settled Bitcoin options on Deribit, in Deribit’s Nov. 24 options data, against 111,797 BTC in the Nov. 27 monthly expiry.

Deribit’s Nov. 24 coin-settled Bitcoin options book showed 6,172 BTC of gross open interest in the daily expiry before PCE and 111,797 BTC in the monthly expiry after it. The exchange publishes open interest with an eight-hour lag.

Source: Deribit options data · Deribit expiry policy · Deribit public API changelog · BEA release schedule

CryptoSlate estimated the effect of removing Wednesday’s expiry using coin-settled contracts expiring within 30 days.

Assuming dealers held the long side of every call and the short side of every put, contracts set to outlast the release accounted for about 93% of the Nov. 24 model’s net negative gamma.

The Nov. 27 expiry alone accounted for about 49% of the original total, leaving about 7% in Wednesday’s expiry under the same assumptions.

The calculation holds prices and positions at their Nov. 24 readings, so actual gamma can shift as Bitcoin moves and expiry approaches, and the public exchange data counts contracts without identifying dealer positions.

The Nov. 27 put open interest was spread across several strikes, including $60,000, $63,000 and $64,000. At the same $60,000 strike, annualized implied volatility was 50.4% for Wednesday’s expiry, 56.1% for Thursday’s and 54.6% for Friday’s.

The higher Thursday and Friday marks cover the inflation release and other risks over longer periods.

A hot print could lift rate expectations and start a selloff that short-gamma dealers reinforce with hedge sales.

A cool print could ease rate pressure and prompt a rebound that the same dealers reinforce by buying. If inflation comes in close to forecasts, the GDP figures and demand for Bitcoin could matter more.

For the rest of the week, watch whether Friday’s expiry changes positioning and whether spot buyers return. The NYSE closes for Thanksgiving, ending Friday’s core equity session at 1 p.m. ET.

If dealers turn long gamma or liquidity improves enough to absorb their trades, the same catalyst could produce a smaller swing.

#5060. NYSE’s Avalanche Pick Hints At XRP’s Role

Home » Trendsetter News » NYSE’s Avalanche Pick Hints At XRP’s Role

NYSE’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily rule out XRP.

The New York Stock Exchange’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily shut out XRP, wealth commentator Kamilah Stevenson argues in her latest video.

Her distinction: settling share ownership and moving money across currencies are separate jobs, and winning one does not automatically secure the other.

According to Dr. Stevenson, Ava Labs announced that Avalanche would provide the core ledger for the clearing firm behind the proposed platform.

She cites Wall Street Journal reporting that Avalanche would be its sole settlement blockchain, with regulatory approval still required.

The proposed venue would support around-the-clock trading and near-instant settlement. Stevenson says NYSE tested Avalanche for roughly a year, prioritizing transaction speed, predictable costs and control over who can participate.

That permissioning capability matters for a regulated exchange. Avalanche (AVAX) can support customized networks with participation restrictions, rather than requiring the exchange to conduct settlement on an unrestricted public network.

AVAX rose as much as roughly 10% on the news, according to the video. Stevenson, who discloses holding the token, calls the selection a win for Avalanche, but cautions against treating infrastructure adoption as proof of investment returns.

“A network being used by a big name and its token being needed” are different things, she says. The announcement, in her account, provided neither revenue figures nor a commitment that NYSE would buy or hold AVAX.

Dr. Stevenson’s XRP thesis centers on overseas investors funding dollar-denominated stock purchases outside conventional banking hours.

A trader holding yen or another currency would need access to dollars or dollar-linked funding before buying U.S. shares.

She argues that this creates an opportunity for cross-border payment infrastructure, including XRP. But it remains a proposed use case, not a disclosed partnership: “I’m not telling you that NYSE is going to pick XRP for that.”

The YouTube video episode does not establish that XRP would be necessary for such funding. Nor does expanded trading access, by itself, demonstrate future demand for the token.

Dr. Kamilah Stevenson also says the platform would support tokenized stocks issued across multiple blockchains, distinguishing asset issuance from the ledger used for settlement.

Those details matter more than a simple Avalanche-versus-XRP contest: the unresolved questions are which services institutions actually adopt, what generates revenue, and whether that activity requires either token.

A historically important signal is back in play.

Macro sentiment is increasingly seeing a 100% probability of an interest rate hike at the next FOMC meeting. September’s 0.3% inflation figure and increasing geopolitical issues have fuelled these concerns.

It now seems investors are bracing for another possible increase in October’s inflation data. Typically, investors respond to this by moving into defensive instruments. Notably, this shift could already be taking place.

Technically, the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) is trending towards 104, which was last witnessed in late Q1. Generally, an increase in the dollar will affect risk assets as the dollar’s yield begins to outshine that of crypto.

But could Solana break this trend, allowing it to maintain its strength against Ethereum?

Solana has started the week on a strong note, with tokenization gaining momentum.

As AMBCrypto reported, weekly trading volume of tokenized equities has recently reached an all-time high of $1.8 billion. Adding to this, the chart above shows that the market cap of tokenized U.S. Treasury bills on the Solana chain rose by $69 million within the last 7 days. This was the biggest increase across all chains.

The timing was telling. Investors appeared to be seeking more secure assets as the dollar strengthened.

Growing interest in tokenized U.S. Treasury bills could fit that defensive shift. Whether it translated into demand for Solana [SOL] remained the missing link.

Solana’s tokenization boom may already be bringing in fresh institutional interest.

According to SoSoValue, weekly ETF flows show a clear gap in investor demand. Solana ETFs saw $4.3 million in inflows last week, while Ethereum ETFs recorded $314 million in outflows. This suggests investors are showing more interest in SOL, adding to the signs that Solana could be gaining ground against Ethereum.

This shift is also visible on the charts. As illustrated in the chart below, the SOL/ETH rate has increased by close to 5% in under two weeks. It is now reaching the levels that it had in late October. And as Solana continues to see an upsurge in its tokenization, it may further strengthen SOL’s position compared to ETH.

Against this backdrop, the rest of Q4 could turn out to be “relatively” better for Solana.

Macro FUD, rising rate hike fears, a stronger dollar, and geopolitical tensions are all adding to the risk of a bearish quarter. However, continued inflows into Solana’s tokenized Treasury market could be an important metric to watch. If this trend continues, it may signal growing investor interest in Solana as broader market conditions remain uncertain.

Solana’s tokenized U.S. Treasury market cap jumped by $69 million in seven days, the biggest increase across all chains.

SOL/ETH gained nearly 5% in under two weeks as Solana ETFs saw inflows while Ethereum ETFs faced heavy outflows.
